slides.prompt: Choose the sentence that makes the ideas flow.
slides.hint: Two stories today: the light bulb, and fast travel.
slides.notes: 60-min Tue lesson 8 Sep 2026, sl_t3 17:50-18:50. Say: 'Eight sentences fell out of two stories. Our job: put back the one that makes the ideas flow.' Module pp.36-37 gapped text (P1P5, marks collected). Outcomes (teacher-kept): use the 4 checks on every gap; complete gaps 1-8 in books. 1M: noisy class, no roles or competitions; fingers vote + brief partner talk only.

slides.prompt: Alina wants to build a robot. Which one is BEST?
options: She joins a robotics class and practises every week.
Her school has a new computer lab.
Many pupils watch robot videos online.
slides.answer: She joins a robotics class and practises every week.
slides.feedback: A connects her goal to the result. B is about the school. C is about other pupils.
slides.notes: Check 1 (topic). Fingers vote 1/2/3, then reveal. Ask: 'Are B and C bad English?' No — good English, wrong job. Module answers stay hidden for the marked bookwork.

slides.prompt: Mei brings home a small kitten. Which one is BEST?
options: She feeds it milk in a warm box.
Kittens like string and soft toys.
Her brother walks to the market.
slides.answer: She feeds it milk in a warm box.
slides.feedback: A follows Mei and the kitten: she is Mei, it is the kitten. B and C drop them.
slides.hint: Who is she? What is it?
slides.notes: Check 2 (who/what chain). Point at she and it as you say them.

slides.prompt: The hall was dark. Then the lamps lit up. Which one is BEST?
options: The electrician had fixed the wires that morning.
Schools hold big events in the hall.
The lamps were made of glass.
slides.answer: The electrician had fixed the wires that morning.
slides.feedback: A explains the change: dark before, light after. B and C only describe the hall.
slides.hint: Use the sentence before AND after the gap.
slides.notes: Check 3 (both sides). The key habit: never read only one side of the gap.

slides.prompt: Razak hates traffic jams. What is his wish?
options: He imagines a machine that moves people instantly.
Buses in his town are old and slow.
Many people take the bus to work.
slides.answer: He imagines a machine that moves people instantly.
slides.feedback: Predict first: he wants instant travel. Only A gives that wish.
slides.notes: Check 4 (predict before options). 30-sec partner talk before voting: 'What does Razak wish for?' Teleportation flavour links to Module p.37 without revealing answers.

slides.prompt: Hakim studies old light bulbs. Which one is BEST?
options: He draws one bulb in his notebook.
Edison was a famous American inventor.
The museum shows many kinds of lamps.
slides.answer: He draws one bulb in his notebook.
slides.feedback: A follows Hakim's work. B shares a name but drops Hakim.
slides.hint: Same word? Wrong question. Which idea connects?
slides.notes: Trap: keyword matching fails. Say: 'Don't ask same word. Ask: which idea connects?' Invention flavour links to Module p.36.

slides.prompt: Found a gap? What do you check?
slides.answer: 1. Topic: what is this part about? 2. Who: who follows who? 3. Both sides: what must join up? 4. Predict the idea, then choose.
slides.notes: Elicit the 4 checks orally first, then reveal to confirm. Leave this slide on screen during bookwork — come back to it while pupils work.

slides.answer: Gaps 1 to 4 use sentences A to D. Gaps 5 to 8 use sentences E to H.
slides.notes: Say: 'First story, first set. Second story, second set.' Then name it: open Module pages 36 and 37. Light Bulb p.36 + Teleportation p.37 (LS 3.1.1/3.1.2). No module answers on slides; books carry the marked activity.

slides.task: Do gaps 1 to 8. Use the 4 checks on every gap.
slides.frame: 1 Topic? 2 Who? 3 Both sides? 4 Predict, then choose.
slides.notes: Say: 'Silent work. Show me the 4 checks on every gap.' Individual marked bookwork, about 20 min. P1P5, 8 marks. Collect books at the door.

slides.prompt: Without looking: what are the 4 checks?
slides.notes: Exit evidence, 2 min: eyes off the screen, tell your partner. Gaps in recall reopen next lesson.
